$comment: Closed vocabulary for Bazaar listings: what KIND of thing a listing sells and which categories of ONE list it belongs to. Compiled into the binary (src/discovery_taxonomy.rs) and resolved per listing at read time into the response-only `kind`, `categories` and `categorySource`, never stored on the record. `categories` below is the whole list: nothing outside it is ever published. A seller's own spelling stays in metadata.category untouched; `aliases` only maps spellings that mean the same thing (keys are compared after lowercasing and turning `_` and spaces into `-`). A raw value with no entry here stays unmapped rather than guessed. `contentCategories` are seller spellings that mean the listing sells content (an article, an essay) rather than a call to a tool. `overrides` is the operator's curation for listings whose own data says nothing usable: host-exact + path-boundary on the parsed https URL (discovery_security::match_manifest_prefix, the matcher the curation manifest uses), each with its evidence. Do not add entries from memory. See docs/plans/bazaar/10-listing-data-and-taxonomy.md.

kinds.api: A tool: a paid call that does something or returns data for the request you send.
kinds.content: A paid piece of content (an article, an essay, a report) that is the same for every buyer. Never boosted above tools by a curated tier.

categories.people: Information about a person: profiles, work email, phone and identity lookups. Returns personal data: whoever buys it answers for having a lawful basis to process it.
categories.company: Information about a company: records by domain, firmographics, who works there.
categories.web-search: Search the open web and get ranked results.
categories.page-read: Fetch, scrape or extract the content of a page you name.
categories.finance: Markets and money outside crypto: stock quotes, FX, financial statements, market data.
categories.crypto: Blockchain and token data: prices, balances, on-chain activity, DeFi.
categories.rpc: Blockchain node access: JSON-RPC methods sent to a chain's node (getLatestBlockhash, eth_call, eth_blockNumber).
categories.human-work: Work done by people on request, with evidence of it: physical errands, on-site checks, data collection.
categories.ai: Model inference and AI agents: completions, embeddings, agent tasks.
categories.data: Datasets and data utilities that fit no narrower category.
categories.developer-tools: Tools for software developers: code, repositories, packages, documentation audits.
categories.security: Security checks, scanning, threat and risk data.
categories.research: Research and analysis produced on request.
categories.reputation: Reputation and trust scores for wallets, agents and services.
categories.infrastructure: Infrastructure for agents and apps: payment facilitation, databases, hosting.

overrides.$evidence: Execution Market, a first-party product (config/bazaar_curation.json): a marketplace where agents pay people to do tasks and return evidence. Its listing in the 2026-10-01T20:03Z catalog snapshot declares metadata.category `execution`, which names the product rather than a category and is left unmapped by the aliases.
Execution Market's task API, the route an agent pays to have a person do a task (config/bazaar_curation.json: bounty-model, ERC-8004-gated).

Paid essays, one per URL. Catalog snapshot of 2026-10-01T20:03Z: 379 listings under this prefix, all self_registered, none declaring a category; the publisher's two other listings on this host (/api/answer, /api/phone-lookup) are tools, outside the prefix, and stay api. The publisher asked, in its Bazaar feedback of 2026-10-01, for the essays to be tagged as content and not as tools; the owner of this facilitator approved it on 2026-10-02.

inference.$comment: Categories for the listings that declare none, from what the listing says about itself: its host, its path, its description and the field names and descriptions of its declared schema (extensions.bazaar). Never tags, never the provider, never a listing that declares any category (a declaration is normalized or left unmapped, never reinterpreted), never content. Each phrase is normalized with the search tokenizer (lowercase, accents and stopwords out, camelCase and letters-then-digits split, light stemming) and matches as consecutive words of one field. A listing scores 2 per distinct `strong` phrase and 1 per distinct `weak` phrase of a rule; a category is assigned when it reaches `threshold`, best first (ties in the order below), at most `maxCategories`. A `fallback` category is assigned only when no other one reaches the threshold. Served as categorySource `inferred`. src/discovery_taxonomy.rs tests every rule against a listing that must match it and one that must not.

upstreams.$comment: The service a listing resells or wraps, so a router can tell ten resellers of one search API from ten search APIs. Closed like the categories: an id below or nothing. Resolved per listing at read time into the response-only `upstream` and `upstreamSource`: `declared` when the seller names it (metadata.upstream, then extensions.bazaar.upstream; an id or a name below, any case), else `inferred`, in this order: the listing's host is one of `hosts` or a subdomain of one; a path segment or a host label equals one of `segments`; a `phrases` entry matches consecutive words of the description. A declaration that maps to nothing is not published and stops inference, like a category. Never inferred for content. `hosts` are each vendor's own domain; a name that is also a common word (perplexity, hunter, apollo, brave) is matched in descriptions only in a form that names the vendor.
